title: Boxty
subtitle: Irish potato pancakes with grated raw and mashed potato
excerpt: Irish potato pancakes made with a mixture of grated raw potato and mashed cooked potato, fried in butter until golden. Dense, substantial, and deeply savoury.
sourceNotes: Florence Irwin, Irish Country Recipes (1937), boxty documented as a traditional Irish potato pancake from Ulster and Connacht. Regina Sexton, A Little History of Irish Food (1998). The traditional rhyme ('Boxty on the griddle, boxty in the pan; if you cannot make boxty, you will never get a man') places it as a cornerstone of Irish domestic cooking.

content.text: Boxty uses two forms of potato: mashed cooked potato for substance and grated raw potato for texture. The raw potato is squeezed dry, mixed with the mash, flour, and buttermilk, then fried in butter. The result is a dense, savoury pancake with a crisp exterior and a potato-rich interior. It is a breakfast dish in Ireland but sits equally well as a side dish for dinner.

items.prepNote: divided: 250 g peeled and boiled for mash, 250 g peeled and raw for grating

content.text: Boil 250 g of the {{potato}} until tender.
Drain and mash until smooth with no lumps.
Grate the remaining 250 g of raw {{potato}} coarsely. Wrap in a clean cloth and squeeze out as much water as possible. Excess water makes the boxty dense and hard to cook through.

Combine the mashed and grated potato in a large bowl. Add {{plain-flour}} of flour, {{buttermilk}} of buttermilk, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt, and pepper. Mix to a thick batter. It should just drop from a spoon.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a heavy pan over medium heat. Drop tablespoons of batter into the pan and flatten slightly. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Fry in batches.

rows.symptom: Pancakes are soggy and fall apart
rows.cause: Raw potato not squeezed dry enough
rows.fix: Squeeze the grated potato very firmly in a cloth until almost no more water comes out. The batter should be thick, not sloppy.

rows.symptom: Pancakes burn on the outside before cooking through
rows.fix: Cook over medium heat, not high. Boxty is thicker than a crepe and needs more time for the heat to reach the centre.

rows.symptom: Batter is too stiff to spread
rows.cause: Potato not starchy enough or too much flour
rows.fix: Add a splash more buttermilk to loosen. The batter should spread slightly when you flatten it in the pan.
Boxty needs generous salt. Taste the batter before cooking and adjust. Use butter rather than oil for frying for the best flavour.

content.text: Boxty comes from the north and west of Ireland, particularly Ulster and Connacht. Potato was the primary staple there, and boxty was part of the daily bread tradition. It appears in Irish cooking books from the nineteenth century alongside griddle bread and soda farls. The two-potato method, mixing mash and grated potato, is what makes boxty unique. It gives a texture that a plain potato cake or a rosti cannot match.
